$comment: TraceRoutine iOS: the App Store Connect declarations that the code makes true, in machine-readable form. The full record, field by field and with dates, is APP-STORE-CONNECT.md (row per key in 'Qué depende de qué'); Google Play's is store/google-play/GOOGLE-PLAY-CONSOLE.md. src/release/appStoreDeclarations.test.ts derives every value below from the code and fails when they diverge. signIn.mode is none | optional | required; when it is not none, signIn.gate names the exported boolean constant that makes the login required (true) or optional (false). localizations are the App Store Connect localizations actually entered (the LISTING.md sections without '· draft, not entered'); uiLanguages are the languages of the binary. record.pending lists every field of this app in App Store Connect that is still unknown or unconfirmed: each line starts with a key that its row in §2–§11 of the record names in backticks, with an Estado that starts with '(verificar)', and every '(verificar)' row there names one of them (account-level checks of §1 and Google Play are only in the record's 'Pendiente de verificar'). weekdayPatternShownAfterDays and trendAfterWeeks are measured by running the stats code; lines of the entered listing that build 1.0.0 (1) does not make true are KNOWN_ISSUES in the test and 'Fallos conocidos' in the record. Public repo: never put API key IDs, issuer IDs, passwords, demo-account credentials or phone numbers here.

pending: appleId: unknown. Angelo reads it in App Store Connect → App Information → Apple ID; then it goes here (declarations.appleId) and as ascAppId in eas.json submit.production.ios, and src/release/storeConfig.test.ts expects it.
submittedForReview: Angelo was told to Save → Add for Review → Submit for Review on 2026-10-21; not confirmed yet (App Store Connect should show Waiting for Review or In Review).
sku: generated by eas submit when it created the record; read it in App Information → SKU and write it in §2 of the record (it is not a secret).
userAccess: eas submit gives Full Access; check it in Users and Access.
regulatedMedicalDevice: whether App Store Connect asked the Regulated Medical Device question (it may not appear for Productivity); if it did, the answer was No.
exportCompliance: that App Store Connect did not ask for export compliance when the build was processed, and that TestFlight shows no Missing Compliance.
testFlightTestInfo: whether TestFlight → Test Information (feedback email, privacy policy URL) was filled in.
internalTesters: who is in the internal group Team (Expo) and that build 1.0.0 (1) shows for them in TestFlight (tester emails are never written in this repo).
